prompt: Write the description for a skill that audits test coverage of the booking capacity invariant.
chosen: Use this skill whenever the user asks to audit, verify, or report test coverage of the booking capacity invariant or fare-rule validators - e.g. 'check invariant coverage', 'capacity test audit', 'are the booking invariants tested'. Also use when preparing a release and coverage of these invariants must be confirmed. Do NOT use for writing new features, running the full test suite, or debugging a single failing test.
rejected: Helps with coverage analysis for the booking system. Use when you need coverage help.

prompt: Write the description for the deploy-checklist skill (verify staging migrations, no held bookings mid-transition, post-deploy capacity dashboards).
chosen: Use this skill whenever a release or deploy is being prepared or requested - e.g. 'prep the release', 'get this ready to ship', 'deploy when green', 'run the deployment checklist'. It walks the pre/post-deploy checks (staging migrations verified, no held bookings mid-transition, capacity dashboards confirmed). Do NOT use for CI configuration changes or for explaining how deploys work.
rejected: Deployment checklist helper. Helps ensure deployments go smoothly.

prompt: Write the description for a skill that converts a repeated manual workflow into a new skill file.
chosen: Use this skill whenever the user wants to CREATE, WRITE, or IMPROVE a skill or reusable workflow - 'make a skill for X', 'automate this workflow', 'why doesn't my skill trigger' - or when they describe a repetitive multi-step task they wish were one command ('every release I re-explain...', 'I keep pasting the same steps...'). Do NOT use for executing existing skills or writing application code.
rejected: A meta-skill for skill management and workflow automation tasks.

prompt: Write the description for a read-only security review agent for sensitive diffs.
chosen: Read-only security and invariant review of diffs and sensitive code paths. Invoke for any change touching booking status transitions, the capacity invariant, fare-rule validators, auth, credential handling, database migrations, or MCP config - and before merging anything on the AGENTS.md ask-first list. Produces findings; never fixes them.
rejected: Security agent. Reviews code for security issues and helps fix vulnerabilities found during review.

prompt: Write the description for an MCP permission audit skill.
chosen: Use this skill whenever an MCP server is about to be connected, reconnected, or have its scope changed - 'connect the database MCP', 'add the GitHub server', 'give the agent write access to X' - and for periodic audits ('is this MCP setup safe', 'review our MCP permissions'). Do NOT use for using an already-connected server's tools, or for application-level authorization questions.
rejected: MCP management skill for server connections and permissions handling.

prompt: Write the description for a task-routing orchestrator skill.
chosen: Use this skill BEFORE starting any task that spans multiple workspaces, touches 3+ files, mixes planning with editing, involves a schema/dependency/deploy change, or is phrased as a feature ('add cancellations') rather than a fix. Also use for 'how should we split this work' or 'can agents do this in parallel'. Do NOT use for single-file fixes, questions, or tasks already decomposed into one concrete step.
rejected: Orchestrates complex tasks. Use for big or complicated work items that need coordination.

prompt: The skill fires on 'run the deployment checklist' but never on 'prep the release'. Fix the description.
chosen: Use whenever a release or deploy is being prepared or requested - 'prep the release', 'get this ready to ship', 'deploy when green', 'run the deployment checklist'. The fix: descriptions must carry the phrasings users ACTUALLY say, verbatim; naming only the artifact ('deployment checklist') matches the author's vocabulary, not users'.
rejected: Use for deployment checklists, deployment preparation, deployment verification, and all deployment-related deployment tasks.

prompt: The review skill fires on every one-line change and floods context. Fix the description.
chosen: Invoke deliberately (not ambient) for diffs touching sensitive paths: status transitions, the capacity invariant, fare rules, migrations, MCP config, or anything on the ask-first list. Do NOT use for copy fixes, renames, comment changes, or diffs confined to test helpers. The fix: heavyweight procedures get explicit negative space AND deliberate invocation - 'whenever code has changed' is every turn of every session.
rejected: Use whenever code has been changed, to review the change, but try to use judgment about when review is really needed.

prompt: Write the description for a fixture-factory skill that creates test data scenarios (e.g. a sailing at capacity 0).
chosen: Use this skill whenever a test needs seed data or fixtures that don't exist - 'I need a sailing at capacity 0', 'create a booking in held status for this test', 'add a fixture for an expired hold'. It generates factory code in test fixture dirs only. Do NOT use to modify seed files, run migrations, or touch any database - fixtures are code, not data writes.
rejected: Test data helper. Creates whatever data your tests need in the database.

prompt: Write the description for a skill that runs the GR-7 color-drift cleanup on a UI package.
chosen: Use this skill when UI colors look inconsistent or off-contract - 'the orange looks different on two screens', 'why are there three shades of blue', 'clean up hardcoded colors', 'make this match the design system'. It greps for color/px literals, classifies each as conformant, drift, or undocumented decision, and replaces drift with token references from design/DESIGN.md. Do NOT use for creating new designs or changing token values.
rejected: Design system skill for color management and visual consistency across the application.

prompt: Write the description for a skill that writes the three-line failure note and manages the reset after a stuck loop.
chosen: Use this skill when an agent or session is stuck - 'we're going in circles', 'this is the third time the same fix failed', 'the agent keeps redoing the same edit' - or automatically after two consecutive failures of the same fix idea. It writes the failure note (tried / failed-how / hypothesis) and stages the context reset. Do NOT use for ordinary debugging that is still making progress.
rejected: Helps when things aren't working. Use if you're stuck or having problems with a task.

prompt: Write the description for a migration-authoring skill (writes migration files; never applies them).
chosen: Use this skill whenever a schema change has been PLAN-APPROVED and needs its migration written - 'write the waitlist table migration', 'add the migration for the approved index'. It edits src/db/migrations/ only and never runs anything: applying migrations is CI's job. Do NOT use before plan approval (schema changes are ask-first), and do NOT use to apply, test-apply, or 'just run it locally'.
rejected: Database migration skill. Handles creating and running migrations for schema changes.

prompt: Write the description for a swarm-launch preflight skill.
chosen: Use this skill ALWAYS before launching parallel agents or an Agent Manager swarm - 'kick off the swarm', 'run these in parallel', 'split this across agents'. It produces the ownership map (agent → exact dirs), mechanically verifies empty intersections, confirms packages/shared is in no zone, and sets the merge order. Do NOT use for single-agent tasks or for monitoring an already-running swarm.
rejected: Swarm skill for parallel agent coordination and multi-agent workflows.

prompt: Write the description for a docs-writer subagent (docs only; instruction files stay human-curated).
chosen: Use for writing or updating documentation under docs/ and package READMEs - 'document the waitlist API', 'update the setup guide'. Proposes (never applies) changes to AGENTS.md or other instruction files as findings, since those stay human-curated. Do NOT use for code comments, commit messages, or design-token changes.
rejected: Writes documentation and keeps all project files up to date, including AGENTS.md and configuration docs.

prompt: Two skills overlap: 'test-writer' and 'invariant-coverage-audit' both fire on coverage asks. Fix test-writer's description to disambiguate.
chosen: Use this skill to WRITE NEW tests - 'add a test for X', 'write cases covering the promotion path', 'we need a regression test for this bug'. Do NOT use for auditing or reporting EXISTING coverage ('check invariant coverage', 'capacity test audit') - that is invariant-coverage-audit's job. The fix: overlapping skills get mutually exclusive phrasing sets; each NOT-clause names the neighbor by its phrasings.
rejected: Use for anything test-related: writing tests, checking tests, coverage, and test quality.

prompt: Write the description for a skill that must also fire for unattended swarm agents preparing releases (no human watching).
chosen: ALWAYS use before any release preparation, whether interactive or as a background/swarm agent - 'prep the release', 'release-check', scheduled release validation runs. Unattended runs have no human backstop, so if any checklist step cannot be verified autonomously, STOP and surface it rather than proceeding. Do NOT use for ordinary feature merges outside a release window.
rejected: Use when the user asks you to help prepare a release and walk through the checks together.
